text:
olivia: Quick thread — following up on the versioning/pinning discussion from last week. We need a compact, queryable metadata shape for model anchoring that handles canaries, absolute pins, and fallbacks without exploding storage or complicating the router.

kenji: TL;dr proposal?

olivia: Proposal sketch: single canonical `model_anchor` object per route with a tiny history. Fields: `active` (id), `overrides` (list of {selector, id, expires_at}), `fallbacks` (ordered ids), `compat_matrix` (version tags). Keep it <= 1KB.

sara: 👍 keeping it small is key. Can we avoid full JSON blobs per request? Router should only need `active` + identifiers for quick decision.

mike: Are `id`s opaque strings or numeric versions? We should pick one. Numeric makes range queries easy, opaque token helps rotate without leaking semantic ordering.

kenji: I vote numeric internal id + human tag. Eg: `{id: 2043, tag: "gpt-like-2043-v2"}`. Router caches map id->binary plan.

olivia: Example schema snippet:```json
{
  "active": "m-2043",
  "overrides": [
    {"selector": "user.team:alpha", "id": "m-2050", "expires_at": "2026-04-01T15:00:00Z"}
  ],
  "fallbacks": ["m-2030", "m-2021"],
  "compat_tags": ["kv-cache-v2", "quantized-8bit"]
}
```

sara: A few concerns: 1) How do we express staged rollouts tied to traffic %? 2) How to represent model family compatibility vs exact model id?

mike: For % rollouts, keep rollout state out of the anchor metadata. Have a separate `rollout_policy` resource referencing the anchor id. That way anchor stays a compact pointer and rollout engine handles traffic splitting.

kenji: For family-level compatibility, `compat_tags` should be expressive enough. Router should match by tag if exact id not available. We also need a fallback resolution algorithm: try exact id -> matching tag -> configured fallbacks -> global default.

olivia: Agree. Also propose a schema version field at top-level `schema_v`. We'll document upgrade rules: no breaking changes without a bump and a 2-month migration window for older private deployments.

sara: How will UI show this? We need resolved effective model for a given selector + time. That implies we need to keep small audit/history entries of overrides (who set it, why). Can we include `meta` with `short_reason` (<=140 chars)?

olivia: Yes include `meta: {actor, reason, change_ts}` but keep it only for override objects not top-level to maintain size.

infra-bot: deploy-hook: anchor-schema-v1.1 applied to staging at 2026-03-20T18:22:00Z :white_check_mark:

mike: Back-compat: router should ignore unknown fields. Also, when `compat_tags` present, we should prefer tags configured as `strict` vs `loose` matching. Suggest tag objects instead of strings: `[{name: "kv-cache-v2", mode: "strict"}]` but that increases size. Maybe default to strict and allow an optional `loose_tags` list.

kenji: Let's keep the common path small: strings. If consumers request full metadata (console/api) we return expanded tag objects. Router gets condensed view.

sara: One more operational thing — when a pin is removed we need an immutable record for audits. Keep overrides history in a separate append-only store keyed by anchor id. Anchor direct object stays tiny.

olivia: Next steps: 1) Kenji to draft a precise JSON schema and example payloads (compact + expanded) 2) Mike to prototype router lookup using `active` + `compat_tags` fallback 3) Sara to prototype UI resolved-view API that joins anchor + history.

kenji: Will do. I'll target a PR with schema and compatibility-guidelines by EOD Friday.

mike: I'll wire up a benchmark to measure extra router lookup latency for tag-matching. Should be <0.5ms on cache hit.

sara: I'll stub the resolved-view endpoint (`/routes/{r}/resolved?selector=user.team:alpha`) and include sample outputs.

olivia: Great. One last note — for private/on-prem deployments we must avoid mandatory background services. Schema must work with just control-plane writes and router caches. Keep polling-friendly fields like `expires_at`.

kenji: Noted. OK wrapping up. If no objections, I'll push schema draft tomorrow morning. :rocket:
